findings.title: Removal listener gated on the V1 flag breaks client deletion under V1+V2 and disables cleanup under V2-only
findings.description:
The diff wraps the whole removal listener in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` (V1). That has two effects:

- **V2-only.** `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` depends only on `AUTHORIZATION` (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/Profile.java:58), so V2-only is a valid setup, and `KeycloakAdminPermissionsServerConfig` uses it. The listener now never runs. Before this diff it did run, and role and group cleanup worked because `MgmtPermissionsV2` does not override `roles()` or `groups()` (MgmtPermissions.java:199-239). Those permission resources now leak when roles or groups are deleted.
- **V1+V2 both on.** `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` (AdminPermissions.java:66-68), so `clients()` is now `ClientPermissionsV2` (MgmtPermissionsV2.java:63-68). Its `setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (ClientPermissionsV2.java:193-195). `DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory.publish` (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory.java:86-90) has no try/catch, and `JpaRealmProvider.java:1006` publishes `ClientRemovedEvent` synchronously, so deleting a client fails. Before this diff, V1+V2 used the base `ClientPermissions` and this worked.

Fix: gate the role and group branches on `V1 || V2`. For clients, either implement V2 cleanup or branch on the evaluator. Add tests for client deletion under V1+V2 and for role/group deletion under V2-only. None exist.

findings.title: `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` never returns per-client grants and can return the literal "Clients"
findings.description:
`findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, …)` matches only resources whose `type` is "Clients" (`findResourceIdByType`, model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/jpa/entities/ResourceEntity.java:64). Per-client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:101-104) without `setType`, so they never match. The only typed resource is the type-level "Clients" resource, whose type is set from its representation (RepresentationToModel.java:1546). When the all-clients grant includes the scope, line 140 adds `resource.getName()`, which is the string "Clients". The caller, `AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:229-230`, then calls `realm.getClientById("Clients")`, which returns null, and then `.getRolesStream()`, which throws an NPE.

Net effect: a per-client `map-roles-composite` grant never shows up in the role-mapping listing, and an all-clients grant produces an NPE. No test covers this method. The scope name passed in (`map-roles-composite`) does match the V2 schema, so the scope name is not the problem.

Fix: enumerate the per-client resources (for example, by server, excluding the type-level resource) or tag them with the type and exclude `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` by name, then map the matches to client IDs. Add a test that grants per-client `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` and asserts the client ID is returned.

findings.title: `canExchangeTo` throws in V2 on a live token-exchange path
findings.description:
`ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Its caller, `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:276`, runs for every non-self target audience. Before this diff, V2 inherited the base implementation. That looks up `client.resource.<id>`, which only V1 `initialize` creates, finds nothing, and returns false, so the client got a clean 403. Now the same request throws an unhandled exception (500). It is reachable with V2 plus `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, and `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` has no feature dependency (Profile.java:76).

The same holds for `isPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, `resource`, and `setPermissionsEnabled` under V1+V2, which the V1-gated endpoints in `ClientResource.java:706-742` reach. That matches the existing `UserPermissionsV2` pattern, so it is acceptable only if V1+V2 is declared unsupported.

Fix: implement V2 `canExchangeTo` (the unused `getEvaluationContext` at line 262 suggests this was the intent) or return false with a debug log. Don't throw on a protocol path.

findings.title: `hasPermission(client, scope)` dereferences a possibly null type resource
findings.description:
When no per-client resource exists, the code passes `getResourceTypeResource(..., "Clients")` straight to `findByResource`. That method returns null when the "Clients" type resource is missing (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:131-133). `PolicyStore.findByResource` says its argument "Cannot be null" (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/store/PolicyStore.java:97), and the JPA implementation dereferences `resource.getId()`, which throws an NPE. The sibling `hasPermission(String)` (lines 244-247) checks for null; this one does not.

This is reachable for realms that enabled V2 before this change. `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:226-228), and it runs only on the enable transition (model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/jpa/JpaClientProviderFactory.java:67-74) or on realm creation/import (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/managers/RealmManager.java:566-573). Those realms never get the "Clients" type resource or the new `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, and `map-roles-composite` scopes. Any admin who lacks the client roles then gets a 500 on client checks. Creating a `configure` permission there fails with `ModelException("No scopes found.")` (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:106-110).

Fix: null-check and return false. Backfill existing realms, or have `init` add missing types and scopes instead of returning early.

findings.title: Per-client and all-clients grants combine inconsistently, so a per-client DENY can be ignored for view
findings.description:
`canView(client)` checks `canView()` first, which includes the type-level VIEW grant, and only then the per-client resource. So an all-clients VIEW grant wins over a per-client NEGATIVE VIEW policy. `canManage(client)` does the opposite: `hasPermission(client, …)` evaluates only the per-client resource when one exists, so the per-client policy shadows the all-clients grant (lines 64-69).

`UserPermissionsV2` uses shadowing for both checks (UserPermissionsV2.java:47-59 and :106-126). The users tests `testViewUserPermission` and `testViewUserPermissionDenyByDefault` assert that a per-user deny overrides the all-users grant. No client test covers a deny. The Javadoc ("Also if the caller has a permission to VIEW all clients") does not describe the shadowing either.

Fix: pick one rule. To match users, the per-client resource should decide when it exists, so `canView(client)` should evaluate it before falling back to `canView()`. Keep role-based checks (`MANAGE_CLIENTS`, `VIEW_CLIENTS`) global. Add deny-override tests for clients and document the rule in `ClientPermissionEvaluator`.

findings.title: Dead code and duplicated evaluation logic in ClientPermissionsV2
findings.description:
Unused members: `logger` (line 51), the `Scope` import (line 27), the `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` static import (line 46), and the private `getEvaluationContext` (lines 262-272, no callers). The scope-matching loop is copied three times (`hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, `hasPermission(String)`, `hasGrantedPermission`). Each copy builds `Arrays.asList(scope)` only to call `contains`. The two `hasPermission` overloads also duplicate the realm/server guards and the evaluation.

Fix: extract one `isGranted(Collection<Permission>, String scope)` helper and one evaluate helper, and delete the unused members. Or implement `canExchangeTo` (see above), which would use `getEvaluationContext`.

findings.title: Javadoc says `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` "return" a value
findings.description: Both methods are `void` and throw `ForbiddenException`. The Javadoc added at lines 95-97 and 100-102 says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.", copied from the boolean methods. Replace it with "Throws ForbiddenException if canView() returns false." (and the matching text for `requireViewClientScopes`). The `canManage(ClientModel)` and `canView(ClientModel)` Javadoc also has a double space before "returns".

findings.title: `getResourceName` has no CLIENTS branch
findings.description:
`getResourceName` resolves a username for USERS resources (lines 310-321) and falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` for everything else. Client resources are created without a display name (lines 101-104), so the policy-resource representation built at `PolicyResourceService.java:218` gets only the raw resource name, which is the client UUID, and no human-readable name. The diff adds the CLIENTS type but not the matching branch.

Fix: add a CLIENTS branch that resolves the client's `clientId` the same way the USERS branch resolves `username`.

findings.title: New V2 client paths lack tests for the behaviors most likely to regress
findings.description:
The new tests cover manage, configure, view, and map-roles for per-client and all-clients grants, which is good. Missing coverage:

- `getClientsWithPermission` (see the FAIL above).
- Token exchange to another client under V2 (`canExchangeTo`).
- Client, role, and group deletion under V1+V2 and under V2-only. The listener FAIL above would have been caught by these.
- A per-client DENY on clients. The users suite has one.

Every test here runs only the V2 config (`KeycloakAdminPermissionsServerConfig.java:28`), so nothing exercises V1 and V2 together.

findings.title: Unused test code
findings.description: The `createClientPolicy` helper added in this diff has no callers. Also, `tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:35` still imports `java.util.Arrays`, whose only use was in the removed `createUserPermission` helper. Remove both, or use them.

findings.title: Style and consistency nits
findings.description:
- Trailing whitespace on the blank line added inside the class.
- Double space in `ClientPermissionsV2.java:214` (`Resource resource =  resourceStore`).
- `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java` has `createUserPolicy(realm, client,"…")` with no space after the comma, in 12 call sites.
- `PermissionClientTest.java:25` imports JUnit 4 `org.junit.Assert.fail`, while the rest of the package uses `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions`. It compiles because `FlowTest` also uses JUnit 4 on the test classpath, but it is inconsistent.
- In `AbstractPermissionTest`, `createPermission(client, resourceId, …)` is an instance method while its sibling helpers are static.

findings.title: `resolveClient` path does not exclude the admin-permissions client
findings.description: `ResourceServerService`, `ScopeService`, and `ResourceSetService` call `throwExceptionIfAdminPermissionClient`. The new CLIENTS branch in `getOrCreateResource` accepts any client ID, including the resource server's own client, so a per-client permission can target the admin-permissions client. I have not confirmed the impact. Confirm the intent, or add the same guard.

findings.title: Per-client lookup owner and scope names are consistent
findings.description: `findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())` matches the owner used when per-client resources are created. `ResourceServerAdapter.getClientId()` returns `getId()` (model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/jpa/store/ResourceServerAdapter.java:91-93), and `getOrCreateResource` creates resources with `resourceServer.getClientId()` (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104). The V2 scope constants (`map-roles`, `map-roles-client-scope`, `map-roles-composite`, `configure`) in `ClientPermissionManagement.java:32-35` match the names in `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS`.
